parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime shows no criminalisation of trans status or gender expression, no documented state targeting, and no universal-exposure measure (no facility bans, registration, or marker-disclosure rule). The exposure is structural: document mismatch carried into every check with no domestic remedy and no stated handling policy (an open question, not a documented adverse practice), protections that name sexual orientation but never gender identity, no relationship recognition, and general LGBTQ stigmatisation. Absence of trans incidents reflects absent monitoring, not safety. No documented acceptance tradition either. Severity if outed is moderate (stigma, service friction, unprotected recourse); nothing supports custody or worse. Thin data and absent protections keep this below the acceptance-with-protections tier.

entry_documents.exposure: Traveller's home passport/visa mismatch with presentation is carried into every border, immigration and hotel check; no domestic gender-recognition remedy and no stated policy on handling the discrepancy.
entry_documents.protection: No documented practice of refusing entry, doubting foreign documents, or sanctioning mismatch; no trans-specific border rule.
entry_documents.interaction: Mismatch could prompt scrutiny that escalates into general questioning, but no documented escalation path exists.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented arrest, detention or custody practice relating to trans visitors; no trans-specific offence exists to charge under.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Same-sex conduct legal since 2012; no cross-dressing, impersonation or morality provision cited against gender presentation.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document mismatch could theoretically feed a fraud framing, but no source records such a pathway.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility-access rule, ward-placement rule or birth-sex segregation policy documented at any level of government.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No documented restriction either; the dossier records no subnational variation.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Any facility placement question on an emergency visit is unanswered rather than adverse.

care_services.exposure: No anti-discrimination protection reaches healthcare; goods-and-services exclusion would have no stated ground of redress for a trans person.
care_services.protection: No documented denial of care to trans visitors; no care-restriction rule cited.
care_services.interaction: Care denial, if it occurred, would fall outside the employment-only protection and outside any named ground.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No gender-identity ground in the labour code or the hate-crime enhancement, so official framing treats a trans person only via sexual orientation; LGBTQ stigmatisation is documented generally.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: UN joint statement signed (symbolic only); employment protection and enhanced sentencing exist for sexual-orientation motivation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: A trans visitor would have to recharacterise their situation as sexual orientation to invoke any stated protection.

minors_guardians.exposure: No documented exposure specific to a travelling parent with a minor; age-of-consent discrepancy (16 vs 18) is unresolved but applies equally regardless of orientation or identity.
minors_guardians.protection: No documented family-related restriction, custody rule or guardian penalty.
minors_guardians.interaction: A mismatched-document parent could face added scrutiny when accompanying a minor, but this is an open question, not evidence.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: LGBTQ people described as facing stigmatisation among the wider population; 2016 poll found 46% would not mind an LGBTQ neighbour — undifferentiated by trans status and a decade old.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No trans-specific violence, killings or police abuse recorded; no organised targeting documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Stigma shapes street reception but no source connects it to documented incidents against visitors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No protection ground names gender identity; no complaints body, no trans-specific machinery, no consular or bilateral arrangement on document mismatch.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Employment and hate-crime provisions exist (orientation only); functioning penal code and courts exist in principle.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse is thin-paper: a visitor could not invoke the labour code and would have no named ground elsewhere.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A: Vellandra operates a routine border register that systematically excludes transgender visitors with no remedy. This dossier documents no entry bar, no register, and no documented adverse border practice — only an unanswered handling question for document mismatch.

Similar in kind, slightly higher: Kestrel Isles shows documented, variable secondary screening and discretionary refusals against trans travellers. Here no such screening or refusal is documented at all; what is shared is uncertainty at the document-check stage and slow/absent remedies.

Closest analogue: a visitor stopped over a document mismatch, briefly held, then released with an apology and compensation after advocacy intervened. This dossier lacks even that documented incident and its working remedy, so it sits a step below, at reduced rather than comfortably documented safety.

Lower than 0.75-C: Meridia trains border staff, recognises trans passport markers, and offers tribunal appeals with compensation. None of that protective machinery — training, recognition, appeals — is documented here; only the absence of criminalisation is shared.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is permissive by omission rather than protective by design. Decriminalisation since 2012, an employment ban and a hate-crime enhancement (both keyed to sexual orientation), and a UN signature are the entire positive inventory, and none names gender identity or reaches a visitor's core exposures: documents, lodging, services, facilities, care. There is no criminalisation of trans status and no documented targeting — so no tier-1 or tier-2 feature — but neither is there any documented acceptance tradition, protective machinery, or record of relief. Document mismatch is a real, continuous exposure whose consequences are simply unstated; thin sourcing means silence is not safety. The result is genuine but unverified everyday safety: moderate severity if outed, unknown enforcement, no recourse that names the traveller. This sits in the reduced-risk band, near its lower edge, and the parent with a minor gains nothing documented either way.
